items.title: Australian jumping spiders show two sleep stages, including REM-like sleep
items.why: Researchers at Germany's University of Bonn filmed the fringed jumping spider, found in northern Australia, at night and found a quiet sleep stage and a REM-like stage with eye movements and twitching. After disturbed nights the spiders spent nearly 80% more time in REM-like sleep. The study is in PNAS.
items.matters: An Australian expert called it the most complete behavioural case for sleep in any arachnid, though brain activity was not measured.

items.title: Israelis vote in first general election since the 7 October attack
items.why: Polls opened at 7am on Tuesday for about 7.3 million eligible voters choosing Israel's 120-seat Knesset. Final surveys showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and an opposition bloc led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party both short of a 61-seat majority. Polls close at 10pm.
items.matters: It is widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu; full results and coalition talks could take days or weeks.

items.title: HSBC profit rises 32% but its shares fall in Hong Kong
items.why: HSBC reported pre-tax profit of $9.6bn for July to September on Tuesday, up 32% on a year earlier, and announced another share buyback of up to $1bn. Revenue from its wealth business was flat, Reuters reports, and the bank's shares fell between 5% and 7% in Hong Kong.
items.matters: Profit was slightly below what analysts expected, and slowing growth in wealth management worried investors, Reuters and TT report.

items.title: Jay-Z to headline the Super Bowl half-time show in February
items.why: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced on 26 October that Jay-Z will headline the half-time show at Super Bowl LXI on 14 February 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Roc Nation, the company he founded, will produce the show.

items.title: Local ceasefire begins in Russian-held Oleshky so aid can reach civilians
items.why: A ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, began early on Tuesday, both sides' militaries say. The White House says Melania Trump brokered it so aid can arrive and civilians can leave; Ukrainian officials estimate about 2,000 people remain.
items.matters: Neither side has said how long it will last; the Kremlin says it could be a model for similar arrangements.

items.title: Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas win the 2026 Ballon d’Or
items.why: England captain Harry Kane of Bayern Munich won the men’s Ballon d’Or at the London Palladium on 26 October, ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal. Spain’s Alexia Putellas won the women’s award for a third time. It was the first ceremony held in London.
items.matters: Kane is the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001; he scored 73 goals for club and country last season.

items.title: Church says 60 Orthodox Christians killed in attacks in Ethiopia's Oromia
items.why: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church says at least 60 of its members were killed in attacks on villages in the Arsi Zone of the Oromia region on 20 and 24 October. A local official blamed a rebel alliance that includes the Oromo Liberation Army, which denies attacking civilians.
items.matters: Oromia's regional government has pledged to pursue those responsible; the church says such attacks have been increasing.

items.title: Walter Koenig, Chekov in the original Star Trek, dies at 90
items.why: The American actor Walter Koenig died on Sunday night, 25 October, at his home in North Hollywood, Los Angeles, his representative said. He played Ensign Pavel Chekov in the 1960s Star Trek series and seven films, and later Alfred Bester in Babylon 5.

items.title: Chris Brown given suspended sentence over London nightclub attack
items.why: The American singer Chris Brown was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for a year, at Southwark Crown Court in London on 26 October. He had pleaded guilty to affray after hitting a man twice with a bottle at a Mayfair club in 2023.

items.title: Brazil's shares and currency fall sharply after Lula wins re-election
items.why: Brazil's main stock index, the Bovespa, fell about 14% on Monday, its biggest one-day drop since 1998, Reuters and AP report, and trading in São Paulo was halted for 30 minutes. The real lost between 8% and 12% against the dollar after President Lula da Silva won Sunday's run-off.
items.matters: Investors had bet on a win for Flávio Bolsonaro and now worry about government spending and debt, analysts say.

items.title: Anthropic files to sell shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT
items.why: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, publicly filed for a stock market listing in the US on Monday. Its filing shows revenue of $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 and a net loss of $80.7 billion, mostly from a non-cash charge. No valuation was given.
items.matters: It could be one of the largest share sales ever; reports say the listing is aimed for mid-November.

items.title: Meta sells about $35 billion of shares to pay for AI
items.why: Meta, owner of Facebook and Instagram, launched share sales worth about $35 billion on Monday to pay for data centres and AI chips, and plans up to $60 billion more from 2027. Chipmakers Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom have said they may buy up to $5 billion of the shares.
items.matters: Meta expects to spend $135bn to $145bn this year, mostly on data centres and chips, The Next Web reports.

items.title: Egypt's pound falls to a record low of 56 to the dollar
items.why: The Egyptian pound fell to a record 56 per US dollar on Monday, LSEG data cited by Reuters show, having first passed 55 on 22 October. Analysts quoted by Enterprise blame foreign investors selling Egyptian debt, costly energy and wheat imports, and regional conflict.
items.matters: A weaker pound makes imported food and fuel dearer in Egypt; the central bank decides on interest rates on Thursday.

items.title: Nurse killed while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
items.why: Attackers killed a nurse and badly injured another responder in Bafwasende, in DR Congo's Tshopo province, on Saturday. Health officials say the attackers accused them of spreading Ebola, which officials call a rumour. The WHO and UN condemned the attack.
items.matters: Attacks on health workers are slowing the response to Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak, officials say.

items.changed: Updated: now a very severe storm; about 50,000 people in shelters, officials say
items.title: Cyclone Arnab nears India's east coast as thousands are evacuated
items.why: Very severe Cyclone Arnab is expected to cross Andhra Pradesh's coast near Yanam on the morning of 28 October, with gusts up to 140 km/h, India's weather office says. State officials say about 50,000 people were in shelters by Monday night, of 400,000 who may need to move.
items.matters: Red alerts cover coastal districts; schools are shut, trains cancelled and coastal roads closed ahead of landfall.

items.changed: Updated: Jordan strikes Syria; Syria says civilians were killed
items.title: Jordan strikes southern Syria after deadly Karak church attack
items.why: Jordan's military says its jets hit armed groups' hideouts in southern Syria on Monday, after Friday's attack on a funeral at a church in Karak killed nine people. Syria's civil defence says seven civilians died, including three children, and Damascus says it was not consulted.
items.matters: Jordan arrested three suspects in the church attack on Monday; Syria has closed its main border crossing with Jordan.

items.title: Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies at 46
items.why: The Canadian-born voice actor Eric Bauza died suddenly on Sunday 25 October, his manager said. He was the modern voice of Looney Tunes characters including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig and Tweety, and won three Children's and Family Emmy awards.
items.matters: His voices reached children around the world through Looney Tunes cartoons, films and games.

items.changed: Updated: talks end with agreement to keep talking; Iran says the US is 'not serious'
items.title: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials hold Tehran talks without breakthrough
items.why: Saudi Arabia's defence minister, Pakistan's army chief and Turkey's intelligence chief met Iran's president and security chief in Tehran on Monday. Iranian state media say the sides agreed to continue talks. Iran's foreign ministry said the same day that the US was 'not serious' about negotiations.
items.matters: Saudi Arabia says the visit aimed to calm the crisis, as President Trump weighs further strikes on Iran.

items.title: Oil eases from six-month high as Qatar mediates with Iran
items.why: Brent crude fell about 1–2% on Monday to around $115 a barrel, after Qatari mediators visited Tehran on Sunday to try to ease tensions with the US, Reuters reports. Brent had risen more than 6% last week, its highest weekly close since 2022.
items.matters: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep supply worries alive, Reuters reports, so fuel and shipping costs stay high.

items.changed: Updated: Bolsonaro's party accepts the result
items.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Lula's re-election in Brazil
items.why: Brazil's Liberal Party said on Monday it recognised the result of Sunday's run-off, which Lula won with 51.8% of valid votes to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2%. Bolsonaro, who called the result 'unacceptable', now says he will ask the courts to revoke Lula's ticket over alleged abuse of power.
items.matters: President Trump said the vote 'looked like another rigged election'; Brazil's vice-president called his remarks 'unfounded'.

items.title: Serbia's Vučić concedes election defeat to student-led movement
items.why: Aleksandar Vučić conceded on Sunday night that his Serbian Progressive Party had lost the snap parliamentary election to the Student List, which grew out of two years of anti-corruption protests. Vučić said early results gave the students 135 to 140 of 250 seats. Turnout was close to 70%.
items.matters: Final official results are still to come, election officials say.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli wins US Grand Prix and nears first Formula 1 title
items.why: Italy's Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes won the United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, on 25 October, his ninth win of the season. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was second and Red Bull's Max Verstappen third. Antonelli now leads by 123 points with 125 left to win.
items.matters: A top-nine finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November would give him the drivers' title, Sky Sports says.

items.changed: Updated: SpaceX's filing shows an Apollo-run fund will buy the chips and lease them to it
items.title: SpaceX signs $40 billion deal to lease AI chips from Apollo-run fund
items.why: SpaceX said in a filing on Monday that a fund managed by Apollo Global Management will buy about $40 billion of Nvidia AI chips and servers and lease them to it for about five years from 2027. Elon Musk had called it a $40 billion debt deal on Sunday.
items.matters: Musk warned that lenders are shunning 'neocloud' firms that only rent out AI computing power, predicting many will fail.

items.changed: Updated: police now say at least 58 died
items.title: Police say 58 killed in gunmen's attack on Nigerian village
items.why: Armed men attacked Binnari village in Nigeria's Taraba State during its market day on Friday. Taraba police say at least 58 people died, including 15 who drowned when a canoe capsized as they fled. Police had first confirmed 10 deaths.

items.changed: Updated: latest DR Congo count from ECDC; Kenya releases first contacts from quarantine
items.title: Uganda orders Ebola quarantine as Congo's case count nears 10,000
items.why: Uganda says citizens returning from DR Congo must quarantine for 21 days at their own cost. Europe's disease agency, ECDC, counts 9,964 confirmed cases and 4,851 deaths in DR Congo by 25 October. Kenya, with nine cases, has released its first contacts from quarantine.
items.matters: Kenya's and Nigeria's first patients both passed through Uganda's Entebbe airport, Africa CDC says.

items.title: Mbappé scores twice as Real Madrid beat leaders Barcelona 2-1
items.why: Kylian Mbappé scored in the 41st and 87th minutes as Real Madrid won 2-1 at Barcelona's Camp Nou on 25 October, after Raphinha had equalised. It ended Barcelona's run of nine straight league wins and was their first defeat of the Spanish season.
items.matters: Barcelona still top La Liga on 27 points, ahead of Atlético Madrid on 25 and Real Madrid on 24.

items.title: Shadab Khan's century and record last-wicket stand lift Pakistan past England
items.why: Pakistan were 154 for nine chasing 242 in Lahore on 25 October when Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf added an unbeaten 89, the highest tenth-wicket stand in a winning one-day chase. Shadab made 113 not out as Pakistan won by one wicket.
items.matters: Pakistan reach the tri-series final on 31 October; England must beat Sri Lanka on 29 October to stay in contention.

items.title: Storms Boelo and Austen leave over 150,000 European homes without power
items.why: Two storms crossed north-western Europe within 24 hours over the weekend. Scottish police say a man died when a tree fell on him in Dumfries and Galloway on Sunday. More than 150,000 homes in the UK, France and Germany were without power on Sunday, AFP reports.
items.matters: Flood warnings remain in parts of Scotland and England, and travel by rail, ferry and air was disrupted.

items.changed: Updated: death toll now 389, with 126,166 admitted to hospital this year
items.title: Bangladesh's dengue death toll this year rises to 389
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported five more dengue deaths and 2,218 hospital admissions in the 24 hours to 8am on 26 October, a day after a record 2,249. This year's toll is 389 deaths, 144 of them in October, with 126,166 people admitted to hospital.
items.matters: Dengue usually peaks in Bangladesh's June–September monsoon, but this year cases are still rising in late October.

items.changed: Updated: Valkyries win Game 5 to lead the series 3-2
items.title: Valkyries beat Dream 64-55 to lead WNBA Finals 3-2
items.why: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 64-55 in San Francisco on Monday 26 October to lead the best-of-seven WNBA Finals 3-2. Kiah Stokes scored 13 points with three blocks; Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 20.
items.matters: One more win, in Game 6 in Atlanta on Thursday 29 October, would give the Valkyries their first title.

items.changed: Updated: UN rights chief warns of 'ethnic cleansing' concerns as displacement rises
items.title: UN rights chief says Israel's Hebron operation must end
items.why: Israel's operation in Hebron, begun after two soldiers were killed at a nearby checkpoint on Friday, has displaced 3,189 people, the city's municipality says. UN rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday threats to empty neighbourhoods 'raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing'.
items.matters: Defence Minister Israel Katz has said residents cannot return until the army finishes; West Bank crossings are shut for Israel's election.

items.changed: Updated: shares allotted; trading starts on Wednesday
items.title: India's Jio Platforms to start trading on Wednesday after record share sale
items.why: Jio Platforms, Mukesh Ambani's telecoms and digital firm, finished allotting shares on Tuesday after its $3.2bn (₹30,213 crore) share sale. Investors bid for more than 22 times the shares on offer, and Indian exchanges recorded more than 10 million applications, a record.
items.matters: Shares start trading on India's NSE and BSE exchanges on 28 October, valuing the company at about $108bn.
